sample.name: OpenSquilla
sample.kind: pure Python wheel containing an LLM gateway, tool runtime and Vue UI

comparison.pypi_all_wheels_attempt: Both exact PyPI versions returned 404; browser fallback failed. Forager recovered the original 0.5.6 wheel from its documented GitHub release asset. No reconstruction was used.
comparison.decisive_evidence: opensquilla/tools/builtin/shell_policy.py is byte-identical in both original wheels (SHA-256 1fddf774659de443ffc49a378a99741b04ada13ce8d716a249fe407fd01f44c8). Its /dev/sda regex and Clear-Disk disk-wipe comment are refusal-list data. SafeBinPolicy.check searches each denylist regex against the supplied command and returns allowed=False on a match; it never launches or overwrites anything.
other_diff_evidence: __init__.py lazily resolves installed package version and has no acquired executable payload.
Added session/content-read contracts, video-generation adapters, desktop cleanup, usage metering, and proxy-aware observability client.

Shell caller checks check_safe_bin and raises ToolError on a denied result in normal mode. Explicit full-host mode bypasses safety preflight, an ordinary advertised dual-use feature; no claim that all modes enforce the policy.
Telemetry posts version/OS/install identity and aggregate usage to product endpoints under privacy controls; HTTP proxy changes preserve TLS configuration.
Base64 attachment decoding creates Blob/image thumbnail data; Python attachment decoding validates size and hashes decoded data. No executable stage was identified in these paths.

Vite source map contains 1016 sources with contents, allowing review of minified code; data-URI SVGs, document parsers and UI code explain encoding/build signals. Both ONNX model assets and all 27 WOFF2 font assets match 0.5.6.
2457 wheel RECORD entries verify; no .pth/native executable startup additions. RECORD integrity is not a trusted publisher signature.
The PDF chunk source map identifies its sole source as pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.mjs, consistent with the new document-preview parser assets.
comparison.queue_discrepancy: With the current rules, the recovered 0.5.6 wheel also fires disk-terms once. The earlier clean queue result does not reproduce; the flagged source was not introduced in 0.5.7.

judgment_basis: The actual flagged path prevents destructive commands, and the reviewed release changes implement the documented agent/UI lifecycle. Ordinary explicit shell execution, network access and telemetry are retained as analyst observations. No concealed unauthorized execution, theft or destruction was established.
limits: No host deployment configuration or authorization was supplied. Dangerous agent capabilities can be misused.
Static review did not execute package code or every downloadable optional toolchain; normal source-analysis flow-budget limitations remain.
Verdict concerns the supplied wheel, not all possible provider endpoints, installed dependencies or runtime tasks.

rules.addition: micro-behaviors/process/create/shell/guard::python-regex-denylist-refusal: notable structural match for denylist iteration, same-pattern re.search, and an immediate sole return of allowed=False in the matched branch.
rules.narrowing: objectives/impact/wipe/disk/term::disk-terms excludes the proven refusal branch, which contradicts the destructive-intent inference from terminology. No filename or product-name allowlist.

relocation.matcher_scope_severity: Unchanged matcher, platforms, types, confidence, notable severity and resource-only DLL exclusion. The phrase is an erasure reference, not an attacker objective. Its consuming composite is updated.

rules.consumer_audit: Exact and ancestor directory consumers inspected for the old phrase and new shell-guard member. Existing fs ancestor consumers are resource-observation profiles; operation-specific attack rules remain independent. Tests include refusal plus a real wiper.

checks.focused: Six cases passed via check.py, copied to scratch to avoid unrelated test-path exclusions.
checks.retained_attack_coverage: Every finding in all four existing controls, including archive members, is preserved after accounting for the one-to-one phrase ID relocation.
near_misses: allowed=True does not qualify as refusal
testing an unrelated regex does not qualify as refusal
executing a command before returning denial does not qualify as refusal
no disk-wipe phrase does not match erasure terminology
checks.mixed_behavior: A refusal policy plus the existing mounted-device dd-wiper fixture still fires the hostile source-mounted-argv-wiper rule.

marker_body: OpenSquilla 0.5.7: denies disk wipes; fixed policy false positive

rescan.classifier_comparison: Calibrated level remains -1 (unflagged), route classes remain 0; aggregate probability 0.8603412 is unchanged. The removed suspicious static rule was not a newly introduced package behavior.
rescan.loss_explanation: Only the incorrect suspicious disk-terms inference and its two now-unreferenced component grouping findings disappear. Underlying disk-erasure phrase (relocated), device-path reference, execution, networking and encoding observations remain. No operation-specific attack finding was lost in the sample or positive controls.
rescan.rule_classifier_disagreement: No hostile or suspicious rule remains. No remaining calibrated classifier alert disagrees with BENIGN; high aggregate member probability remains, and the installed v18 model warns it omits newer v21 features.
